---
title: Observability
---

`@opentelemetry/api` is a peer dependency. Applications register their own tracer and meter providers; without a provider, the instrumentation is a no-op.

Subject operations emit `xstate.nats.subscribe`, `xstate.nats.message`, `xstate.nats.publish`, and `xstate.nats.request` spans. NATS reconnect events emit `xstate.nats.reconnect`; KV watches emit `xstate.nats.kv.watch` and `xstate.nats.kv.entry`. Publish/request operations inject trace context into NATS headers; received messages extract it so traces can cross application boundaries.

## Lifecycle diagnostics

```ts
config: {
  opts: { servers: ['wss://your-nats.example'] },
  maxRetries: 3,
  diagnostics: { lifecycle: true },
}
```

When enabled, root transitions emit sanitized `xstate.nats.lifecycle` spans and console breadcrumbs with state, event type, server URLs, retry count, auth type, and manager readiness. Raw protocol debugging is separate from lifecycle diagnostics.

## Credential instrumentation

Credential load/refresh spans are `xstate.nats.credentials.load` and `.refresh`. Metrics are:

| Metric | Kind |
|---|---|
| `xstate.nats.credentials.operations` | Counter by operation/outcome |
| `xstate.nats.credentials.operation.duration` | Duration histogram in milliseconds |
| `xstate.nats.credentials.state.transitions` | Counter by state |

Set `credentials.diagnostics: true` for sanitized credential state/operation breadcrumbs. Credential contents and provider error messages are excluded from credential instrumentation. The browser demo's State panel likewise summarizes state and counters without dumping auth configuration.
